newsitem.title: GERMANY: Welteke-Euro bank should introduce minimum reserve.
newsitem.headline: Welteke-Euro bank should introduce minimum reserve.

text.p: A German Bundesbank council official said on Monday that the European Central Bank should introduce minimum reserves and that this should not give non-EMU finance centres any competitive advantage.

"Non-EMU central banks should not be allowed to be obtain overnight funds in euros at the same rates as those within currency union," said Ernst Welteke, adding that those who sought such conditions were hoping to cherry-pick.

"I see a good chance that Frankfurt will become the European continent's most important financial centre," Welteke, who is also president of the central bank of the state of Hesse, told foreign journalists.
He added that the new body aimed at promoting Frankfurt as a financial centre, Finanzplatz Frankfurt eV, would help clear up what some called Frankfurt's "image problem."
Welteke was speaking at a dinner organised by the International Business Journalists Forum.
